title: HashMap cache concurrency issues — infinite loop, lost updates, thread-safe alternatives
shortTitle: What concurrency issues does HashMap cause?

s1_definition.profdef: A plain `HashMap` used as a cache in a multi-threaded service causes: (1) **Infinite loop** (Java 7) — concurrent resize creates a circular linked list in a bucket → `get()` loops forever → CPU 100%, thread hangs. (2) **Lost updates** (Java 8+) — two threads put simultaneously → one put overwrites the other → data lost. (3) **Stale reads** — no visibility guarantee → thread reads outdated value. (4) **ConcurrentModificationException** — iterating while another thread modifies. Thread-safe alternatives: `ConcurrentHashMap` (best — per-bucket locking, lock-free reads, atomic operations), `Collections.synchronizedMap(new HashMap<>())` (simpler but coarse — one lock for everything), `Caffeine`/`Guava Cache` (with TTL, eviction, stats).
s1_definition.analogy: A plain HashMap cache = a shared WHITEBOARD with no rules. Two tellers write at the same time → one overwrites the other → account data LOST. Worse (Java 7): two tellers reorganizing the whiteboard simultaneously → create a LOOP in the layout → anyone reading gets stuck walking in circles FOREVER (infinite loop, 100% CPU). Fix: `ConcurrentHashMap` = whiteboard with per-section locks. Two tellers writing to DIFFERENT sections → both proceed. Same section → one waits briefly.
s1_definition.oneliner: HashMap + threads = infinite loop (Java 7), lost updates, stale reads. Fix: ConcurrentHashMap (per-bucket lock, lock-free reads, atomic computeIfAbsent). NEVER HashMap in multi-threaded code.
s1_definition.raw:

(2) **Lost updates** (Java 8+) — two threads put simultaneously → one put overwrites the other → data lost. (3) **Stale reads** — no visibility guarantee → thread reads outdated value. (4) **ConcurrentModificationException** — iterating while another thread modifies. Thread-safe alternatives: `ConcurrentHashMap` (best — per-bucket locking, lock-free reads, atomic operations), `Collections.synchronizedMap(new HashMap<>())` (simpler but coarse — one lock for everything), `Caffeine`/`Guava Cache` (with TTL, eviction, stats).

**In simple words (banking analogy):** A plain HashMap cache = a shared WHITEBOARD with no rules. Two tellers write at the same time → one overwrites the other → account data LOST. Worse (Java 7): two tellers reorganizing the whiteboard simultaneously → create a LOOP in the layout → anyone reading gets stuck walking in circles FOREVER (infinite loop, 100% CPU). Fix: `ConcurrentHashMap` = whiteboard with per-section locks. Two tellers writing to DIFFERENT sections → both proceed. Same section → one waits briefly.

**One line to remember:** HashMap + threads = infinite loop (Java 7), lost updates, stale reads. Fix: ConcurrentHashMap (per-bucket lock, lock-free reads, atomic computeIfAbsent). NEVER HashMap in multi-threaded code.

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The balance cache service used `HashMap` for 50K account balances.** Under 200 concurrent threads: (1) Two threads inserting simultaneously → lost 500 balance updates per day. (2) Thread reading during resize → infinite loop on Java 7 (CPU spike to 100%, service unresponsive for 30 seconds). (3) Thread reading stale cached balance → processed a withdrawal against an outdated balance → overdraft. Fix: `ConcurrentHashMap` — per-bucket locking for writes, lock-free reads, atomic `computeIfAbsent` for cache-miss loading. Zero lost updates, zero infinite loops, zero stale reads.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1 (HashMap — broken).** 100 threads put 100 entries each. Two threads hash to same bucket simultaneously → one put lost. Result: <10000 entries.

**Step 2 (ConcurrentHashMap — safe).** Same 100 threads. Per-bucket locking → each put atomic within its bucket. Different buckets: parallel. Result: exactly 10000.

**Step 3 (computeIfAbsent).** 50 threads request "SAV2001" simultaneously. First thread: key absent → loads from DB → caches. Other 49: key present → return cached. DB called ONCE (atomic).
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ HashMap PROBLEMS (multi-threaded) ═══

  Java 7: resize → circular linked list → get() infinite loop → 100% CPU!
  Java 8: concurrent put → lost updates → entries missing!
  Both:   no visibility → stale reads!
          iteration + modification → ConcurrentModificationException!

  ═══ ConcurrentHashMap FIXES ═══

  Per-bucket lock: two threads, different buckets → parallel!
  Lock-free reads: get() uses volatile → always fresh!
  Atomic ops: computeIfAbsent, merge, compute → no race!
  Weakly consistent iterator: no CME!
```

sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — Thread-Safe Cache Alternatives ═══

  ┌─ HashMap (NOT thread-safe!) ──────────────┐
  │  No locks. No volatile. No atomic ops.     │
  │  Concurrent put → lost updates             │
  │  Concurrent resize → infinite loop (Java 7)│
  │  NEVER use in multi-threaded code!         │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌─ ConcurrentHashMap (BEST) ────────────────┐
  │  Per-bucket sync (Java 8: CAS + sync)     │
  │  Reads: lock-free (volatile)              │
  │  computeIfAbsent: atomic load-if-missing  │
  │  merge: atomic accumulate                  │
  │  No null keys/values                       │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌─ synchronizedMap (simple, slow) ──────────┐
  │  ONE lock for entire map                   │
  │  Every op: lock → do → unlock              │
  │  Iteration: must sync externally!          │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌─ Caffeine (production cache) ─────────────┐
  │  Thread-safe + TTL + eviction + stats     │
  │  cache.get(key, loadFn) → atomic!         │
  │  Best for: expiring caches with metrics   │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A plain HashMap is NOT thread-safe — using it as a cache in a multi-threaded service causes: infinite loops during concurrent resize (Java 7 — CPU 100%, thread hangs), lost updates (Java 8+ — two puts race, one lost), stale reads (no visibility guarantee), and ConcurrentModificationException during iteration. The fix is ConcurrentHashMap: per-bucket locking for writes (fine-grained, high concurrency), lock-free volatile reads (zero lock overhead), atomic compound operations (computeIfAbsent loads from DB exactly once even with 50 concurrent requests for the same key).

For production caches: Caffeine or Guava Cache add TTL, size-based eviction, and metrics on top of thread safety. `Collections.synchronizedMap()` works but uses one coarse lock for everything — poor concurrency under load. In banking: balance cache with HashMap → 500 lost updates/day + occasional infinite loop → ConcurrentHashMap → zero lost updates, zero loops, atomic cache loading.
